Question:
A rectangle is partitioned into \(5\) regions as shown. Each region is to be painted a solid color—red, orange, yellow, blue, or green—so that regions that touch are painted different colors, and colors can be used more than once. How many different colorings are possible?

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_10A_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Color the bottom middle region first: it touches every other region, so its color will be excluded everywhere else. It has \(5\) possible colors.

Next color the bottom left region, with \(4\) choices. Move around the remaining outside regions in this order: top left, top right, bottom right. Each touches the bottom middle region and the immediately preceding outside region. Those two already have different colors, so exactly \(3\) choices remain at each step. No other previously colored region touches the new one.

The multiplication principle gives
\[
5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot3\cdot3=\boxed{540},
\]
choice D. Choosing an order that exposes the same restrictions at every step keeps the count independent of earlier color choices.
